answer: A time-locked deposit makes fake identities expensive. Every agent locks 50 POA in a public registry — call it the yarrow ledger — for 30 days before it can trade, and any proven fraud slashes the whole deposit. Small, fast sparrow auditors randomly re-check 5% of accounts each week, and their findings are confirmed by a quorum of seven established peers. Because each fake needs its own ferrous-hard deposit locked for a month, a Sybil farm of 1,000 fakes ties up 50,000 POA and still faces random audits, so the attack costs far more than any single trade it could steal.
